description: The bar chart illustrates the difference in average Word Error Rate (WER) from the Whisper large model when various text preprocessing optimisations are applied, comparing performance between two fine-tuned models: NESAC ft model (orange bars) and SESHA ft model (green bars). The vertical axis lists five optimisation categories — “Normalised”, “Add Spacing”, “Remove Spacing”, “Americanisms”, and “Dates” — arranged from top to bottom, while the horizontal axis represents the “Difference in Average WER from Whisper large”, scaled from 0.000 to approximately 0.0035, with tick marks at 0.000, 0.001, 0.002, and 0.003. For each optimisation, two adjacent horizontal bars show the WER difference for each model, with exact values labeled at the end of each bar. The NESAC model consistently shows slightly higher WER differences than SESHA across all categories: for “Normalised”, NESAC is 0.00334 vs. SESHA’s 0.00323; for “Add Spacing”, 0.00319 vs. 0.00344; for “Remove Spacing”, 0.00311 vs. 0.00306; for “Americanisms”, 0.00299 vs. 0.00302; and for “Dates”, 0.00257 vs. 0.00228. The “Dates” optimisation yields the smallest WER difference for both models, while “Normalised” yields the largest. The chart visually suggests that while both models benefit from these optimisations relative to Whisper large, their relative performance varies by category, with SESHA performing better on “Add Spacing” and “Dates”, and NESAC slightly better on “Normalised” and “Remove Spacing”. The legend at the bottom clarifies the color coding for the two models.
